`lib/application.js`
This one file contains the whole mechanism: `app.use` for mounting, the `'mount'` listener that sets prototypes for inheritance, and `app.handle`, which restores the prototypes on each request.

The `app.use()` method (around line 219) attaches a child app under a path by registering a `mounted_app` wrapper on the router and setting `mountpath` and `parent`. The `'mount'` listener (lines 109–122) makes the child inherit from the parent by calling `Object.setPrototypeOf` on the child's `settings`, `request`, `response` and `engines`, so lookups fall through to the parent.

The `protocol` getter in `lib/request.js` (line 297) starts from the socket: `this.socket.encrypted` gives `https` or `http`. It only consults `X-Forwarded-Proto` if the `trust proxy` check passes for the socket's remote address, and then it uses the first value in that header. `lib/application.js` (lines 370–371) is where the `trust proxy` setting is compiled into the trust function that check calls.

Why: the TLS fact comes from the socket, but the value is only overridden by the forwarded header when the immediate peer is a configured trusted proxy, so a client can't spoof `https` by sending the header itself.
